chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from a number of his companions, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The divorce of the young boy is valid when he has attained intellect, and so is his bequest and his charity, even if he has not yet undergone seminal emission.

key_terms.الْغُلَامِ: The young boy (pre-pubescent or young male)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a young boy's divorce and bequest in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the threshold of legal capacity (ahliyyah) for minors, asserting that intellectual maturity ('aql) suffices for valid divorce, bequest, and charity, independent of physical puberty (ihtilam). In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction underscores that cognitive discernment, rather than mere biological development, is the primary criterion for exercising civil rights and obligations.
